title: Regional Manager: Fleet
text:
Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time.
With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Belonging at Absa
Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities. We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Job Summary
To lead sustainable regional growth and protect the value of the existing customer portfolio through an equally weighted focus on business development and customer relationship management. The Regional Manager is accountable for new business acquisition, customer retention, increased share of wallet, revenue growth and profitability across the region. These outcomes are delivered through the leadership, coaching and performance management of a team of Business Development and Customer Relationship Consultants, supported by effective collaboration with internal product, credit, risk, operations and service teams. The role owns the regional customer lifecycle from prospecting and acquisition through onboarding, relationship deepening, service recovery, renewal and retention, positioning AVMS as the preferred fleet management and vehicle leasing partner.
Job Description
Regional Business Development & Market Growth
• Translate the AVMS strategy into a regional sales and customer growth plan with clear segment, production, revenue and profitability priorities.
• Build and maintain a balanced regional pipeline across Corporate, SME and Public Sector markets through proactive prospecting, networking, referrals and strategic partnerships.
• Lead the team through the full sales lifecycle, including needs analysis, solution design, pricing, proposal development, negotiation, closure and implementation handover.
• Achieve regional new business production, revenue, margin and market-share objectives within approved pricing, credit and risk parameters.
Customer Relations, Retention & Portfolio Growth
• Own the health, retention and growth of the regional customer portfolio with the same level of focus as new business acquisition.
• Implement a structured customer engagement model, including relationship plans, regular business reviews, service performance reviews and executive engagement for priority customers.
• Identify and convert cross-sell, upsell, renewal and fleet expansion opportunities to increase customer share of wallet across AVMS products and value-added services.
• Monitor customer satisfaction, complaints, service risks and early-warning indicators; coordinate timely service recovery and root-cause resolution to prevent attrition.
• Maintain clear retention and growth plans for customers at risk, strategic accounts and high-potential portfolios.
Consultant Team Leadership & Performance Management
• Lead, coach and performance-manage a regional team of consultants accountable for acquisition, relationship management, retention and portfolio growth.
• Allocate customer portfolios, prospects and regional opportunities to ensure clear ownership, appropriate capacity and balanced coverage.
• Set individual and team targets and maintain a disciplined management rhythm covering pipeline, customer plans, renewals, service issues, wallet-growth opportunities and forecast accuracy.
• Build capability in consultative selling, fleet and leasing solutions, commercial acumen, negotiation, customer engagement and service recovery.
• Create a high-performance, customer-led culture with clear accountability, collaboration and succession planning.
Regional Customer & Commercial Governance
• Maintain a consolidated regional view of pipeline, portfolio performance, customer profitability, retention risk, wallet growth and service trends.
• Use customer, operational and financial insights to prioritise interventions and implement corrective action where performance is below plan.
• Ensure accurate forecasting, CRM discipline, management reporting and escalation of material commercial or customer risks.
• Balance customer outcomes, commercial returns and risk when making regional decisions.
Stakeholder Management & Service Delivery
• Coordinate Credit, Risk, Product, Operations, Finance, Legal and Customer Relations stakeholders to deliver integrated customer solutions and resolve regional delivery constraints.
• Ensure seamless onboarding and implementation of new customers, with clear handover, service commitments and accountability.
• Represent the voice of the customer in product, process and service-improvement forums and provide market intelligence to shape AVMS propositions.
Governance, Risk & Compliance
• Ensure adherence to Absa policies, sales governance, delegated authorities and applicable regulatory requirements.
• Maintain complete and accurate approvals, customer records and deal documentation throughout the customer lifecycle.
• Manage customer information in accordance with POPIA and relevant legislation and promptly escalate conduct, service, operational and reputational risks.
Education
Bachelors Degree and Professional Qualifications: Business, Commerce and Management Studies (Required)

title: Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy
text:
Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time.
With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Belonging at Absa
Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities. We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Job Summary
To develop tactical strategy and delivery plans, formulate associated practice/s and to ensure operational implementation and adoption with regards to legal methodology, governance and delivery objectives.
Independently manage complex privacy and regulatory legal matters and translate legal requirements into clear, practical and workable business solutions.
The role requires substantial hands-on data privacy legal experience, including strong advisory, contractual drafting and negotiation capability.
Job Description
Accountability: Legal Risk
• To provide highly specialised legal advice and support to the dedicated area of support.
• Act as a senior legal subject-matter expert on data privacy and data protection law, regulatory and financial crime.
• Review and legally assess Privacy Impact Assessments, compliance assessments, new products, projects, technologies, processes and proposed data-use arrangements.
• Provide independent legal advice on novel and complex data use, data sharing, disclosure, retention, cross-border transfer and related privacy matters across the Bank, the Group and ARO.
• Draft, review and negotiate data protection provisions, data processing and data sharing agreements, consent wording, privacy notices, forms, customer communications and other privacy-related documentation.
Accountability: Leadership & Management
• Build strong client relationships and engage confidently with stakeholders at different levels of seniority, managing complex or conflicting expectations professionally and effectively.
• Independently plan, prioritise and manage a broad portfolio of matters from instruction through to completion, taking ownership and providing clear legal advice, direction and follow-up.
• Contribute to the development and achievement of team objectives and strategy, while providing high-quality support to business and Legal stakeholders.
• Represent the Bank independently as a subject-matter expert at internal committees, governance forums, industry engagements and professional bodies, and supervise others where appropriate.
Accountability: Commercial
• Demonstrate strong analytical skills and solve complex problems creatively and effectively
• Drive good cost-control behaviour, particularly in relation to external legal spend, and consistently deliver against a broad range of competing priorities and deadlines.
• Manage external counsel
• Add value in commercial and technical discussions, translate complex privacy requirements into practical business advice, and provide relevant legal training to internal clients.
Accountability: Risk and Control
• Strengthen Legal’s contribution to the effective identification, management and mitigation of legal risk across the business.
• Promote awareness of, and support adherence to, applicable legal policies and control requirements.
• Build effective partnerships with Risk, Compliance and other key control functions to support coordinated and effective risk management.
Accountability: Teamwork
• Collaborate proactively across teams and geographies within Legal, contributing to the development and achievement of team objectives and helping to break down silos.
• Share knowledge and expertise openly, provide objective and constructive feedback, and contribute to the planning and delivery of Legal Function knowledge sessions.
Accountability: Technical
• Act as a trusted legal advisor to business and infrastructure functions, providing clear, practical advice on relevant legal and market developments and their business impact.
• Proactively monitor domestic and international privacy and regulatory developments, assess their legal and practical impact on the Bank, the Group and ARO, and communicate implications and recommended actions clearly and timeously.
• Represent the Bank as a subject-matter expert at internal committees and industry forums, contributing to industry initiatives and maintaining a strong external professional network.
Preferred Education
BComm Law and LLB; or B A Law and LLB; or B Juris and LLB; BProc or LLB
Preferred Experience
• Admitted attorney qualified to practise in South Africa, ideally with at least five - eight years’ relevant post-qualification experience.
• Substantial specialist legal experience in data privacy and data protection is essential, including hands-on experience drafting and negotiating data protection provisions, data processing agreements and related documentation.
• Experience working in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment and managing competing demands; financial-services experience is advantageous.
• Experience with financial-sector regulatory matters, including market conduct and financial crime, is advantageous.
• Experience advising across multiple jurisdictions, particularly African jurisdictions, and representing an organisation at internal governance and external industry forums is advantageous.
Knowledge and Skills
• Deep expertise in POPIA and relevant domestic and international data privacy and data protection laws, with an understanding of applicable financial-sector regulation and best practice.
• Excellent legal analysis, interpretation, research and drafting skills, including strong contractual drafting and negotiation capability.
• Ability to provide practical, commercially balanced legal advice and to distinguish between legal, compliance, risk, control and operational responsibilities.
• Strong written and verbal communication, influencing and stakeholder-management skills, with the confidence to exercise independent judgement and provide constructive legal challenge.
• Proactive horizon scanning, with the ability to identify, assess and clearly communicate the legal and business impact of relevant developments.
• Highly organised, proactive and deadline-driven, with the ability to manage competing priorities and drive matters to completion with minimal supervision.
• High attention to detail, integrity and reliability.
Education
Bachelor Honours Degree: Law, Military Science and Security (Required)

text:

Job Summary
Lead the agile solution design, deployment & ongoing optimization & evolution of enterprise wide technology products and services (full stack engineering & ownership / control) in low complexity environments.
Job Description
Product & Service Direction Setting, Solution Design & Performance Management
• Work with the CIO & business product owners to define the product & technical strategy (Full Stack – End to End)
• Act as the single point of partnership & assume responsibility for managing the senior business interface (product owner) relationship
• Assume one stop shop accountability for the delivery of the product & solutions (risk cannot be outsourced to vendors)
• Apply design thinking practices to deliver architecturally sound technical product & service solutions (and explain / guide / coach others on this architecture holistically and technically)
• Lead & facilitate the design of the product & or service solution blueprints aligned to the organization strategy (Short, Medium & Long Term)
• Collaborate across the tech value chain (CSO, CTO, etc.) to guide the business on the appropriate technical solution (cost to value) & the range of strategic technical choices to be made
• Lead the detailed scoping, prioritisation & integration planning for the design & deployment of products & services with & across multiple stakeholder groups (Front End, Back End & Integration) – (aligned to solution blueprints)
• Meaningfully contribute & ensure solutions align to the design & direction of the Group Architecture standards, principles, preferences & practices. Short term deployment must align to strategic long term delivery.
• Meaningfully contribute & ensure solutions align to the design and direction of the Group Infrastructure standards and practices e.g. OLA’s, IAAS, PAAS, SAAS, Containerisation etc.
• Strategically & operationally monitor the performance of products and services (all applications) – ensuring ongoing optimization & cost to value for our businesses (think bank wide)
DevOps (with deep knowledge & understanding of context within which we develop architecturally & infrastructurally)
• Leverage the required expert level (own) skill & knowledge in architecture & Infrastructure, design and manage all development & development practices & outputs across squads (apply knowledge on virtualization, containerization, automation, storage & serverless technologies (e.g. AWS, Azure, Google, & on prem-Cloud, etc.)
• Ensure the most optimal design & deployment of technical products and services in the organization (via pipeline – not manually)
• Design & Implement Automation Testing, Continuous Integration & Continuous Delivery Strategies & frameworks across squads for effective solution development & deployment (understand and apply expert knowledge in e.g. Kubernetes, Jenkins, TeamCity, Arifactory, MS Powershell, Collaborative Lifecycle Management (CLM) Tools, APM Tools (e.g. NewRelic & Splunk) etc.
• Ensure solution designs deliver on the key technical principles of: self-service, repeatability, testability, scalability & resilience
• Guide code development practices and processes through an understanding of complex concepts and developmental practices such as threading, parallel processing, asynchronous programming, domain driven design, lambdas etc. & coding language expertise (e.g. Java, C++, Groovy, Python, Bash, Perl, Ruby etc.)
• Guide & ensure the delivery of quality development (code) based on own experience in developing across a range of applications including but not limited to: server side, client side, web (SOAP, REST, JSON), socket based programming, batch & real time, building architectural patterns, security / security domains)
• Effectively manage the DevOps pipeline & associated releases for maximum customer impact & minimum business risk
• Manage the maintenance & optimization of applications, products & services as a ‘way of doing things / culture’ within the development teams. You are fully accountable for the longevity of applications aligned to Group Architectural practices.
• Coach & Mentor senior developers across squads on the technical competencies to effectively deliver on DevOps solutions (see Dev competency model in skills & competencies section). To do this, display proficiency in the Senior level competency requirements.
Delivery Management (where there is a specific product / service you manage)
• With fluency in the deployment of agile methodologies, resource & manage the appropriate number and nature (skill & capability) of squad based teams to execute on both Run & Change elements of delivery
• Work in collaboration with transformation & change teams for effective resourcing and delivery management of various programmes at all levels (SI, BU etc.)
• Ensure agile practices are implemented and sustained for effective delivery to business e.g. RETRO’s etc.
• Positively & proactively manage product owner relationships including building product owner technical capability to enable balanced & best fit decision making
• Proactively engage with & partner CTO, CSO, SE, Risk and broader enablement functions to drive alignment & leading practice in technology design & deployment
People
• Set & Cascade Product & Service direction across squads
• Proactively attract, recruit, develop, retain, reward & deploy a diverse resource base aligned to an ever evolving tech environment (ahead of demand)
• Build a high performance team environment through self-directed teams by driving performance management & measurement that is aligned with agile working practices (including daily, weekly, etc. sprint routines, regular & honest feedback etc.)
• Accountable for the right people in the right teams to deliver on our tech strategy (always!)
• Leverage coaching techniques in all squad related activity to drive a higher quality design and deployment of technical products and services
Financial & Vendor Management, Risk & Governance
• Carry the ‘one stop shop’ accountability for all risk associated with technical decision making (from ideation to deployment)
• Manage & Apply the organization risk & governance frameworks
• Ensure decisions on infrastructure & product design are aligned to chapter & guild guidelines & are sustainable for the enterprise
• Proactively involve / engage chapter & guild leads in product design & infrastructure decision making, applying an enterprise wide lens to product & service development
• Manage all vendor selection processes & take full accountability for all related commercial impact
• Negotiate best fit contracts for the organization at an enterprise level and align decision making to our key business principles of scalability, resilience, captivity etc.
• Deliver on time & on budget (always)

Job Summary

Testing may apply to all or a combination of the following front-end, back-end, integration, performance, scalability and regression testing of solutions. Job Description
QA Engineering

• Actively participate in daily Scrum and project planning meetings.
• Participate and analyze test automation requirements during the requirements analysis phase of technical product & service development, maintenance & optimization (across tribes & squads) – using design specifications and technical documentation (e.g. Business Briefs, User Stories, Architecture & Integration documentation)
• Prepare QA & Automation testing documentation (planning, design, execution and sustainability)
• Develop automation test plans
• Develop and execute automated test scripts using various technologies (automated scripts, test harnesses, SQL scripts etc.)
• Perform various types of automation testing (regression, integration, black box, scalability)
• Evaluate automated test cases and analyse & report results
• Facilitate test plan / case reviews within squads
• Work with product engineers to evaluate software / solution quality & provide recommendations for improvement / enhancement
• Contribute to the design and selection of testing frameworks for business applications

Job Summary
The South Africa Bank Treasurer is accountable for the strategic stewardship of the South African banking entity balance sheet. The role integrates liquidity, funding, capital, HQLA portfolio management, banking book interest rate risk and ALM earnings management to support resilience, regulatory compliance and sustainable risk-adjusted returns.
The role is the budget owner for both the ZAR and USD ALM positions and is responsible for actively steering those positions within approved risk appetite, limits, mandates and governance. The role provides senior Treasury leadership to South African businesses and acts as a key interface with Finance, Risk, business leadership, executive management, regulators and relevant industry forums. The role reports into the Group Treasurer.
Job Description
Key accountabilities
The role oversees major procurement initiatives and drives the development and execution of commercial solutions that deliver significant value for the Group, ensuring alignment with service category and supplier strategies.
Accountability:  Asset Liability Management & Overall Banking Book Interest Rate Risk
•          Own the ZAR and USD ALM budgets and performance.
•          Steer structural interest rate and liquidity positions within approved limits.
•          Optimise net interest income, margin and economic value across the banking book.
•          Oversee IRRBB, including repricing, basis and optionality risks.
•          Use forecasts, scenarios and stress tests to guide positioning and corrective action.
•          Advise ALCO on balance sheet strategy, risk-reward trade-offs and management actions.
•          Assess the capital, liquidity and earnings impact of business plans and transactions.
Accountability:  Liquidity & Funding Oversight and Managing the Interaction with the Global Markets Business
•          Advise on the South African liquidity and funding strategy in normal and stressed conditions and consider contingency readiness.
•          Steer funding mix, tenor, concentration and cost across local and foreign currencies.
•          Set clear mandates and operating boundaries with Global Markets for execution and risk transfer.
•          Coordinate funding, hedging and market activity with Global Markets while retaining Treasury accountability.
•          Oversee the Intra-day Liquidity Desk and related controls.
Accountability:  HQLA Portfolio Responsibility
•          Own and manage the Bank’s HQLA portfolio within approved mandates and liquidity requirements.
•          Set asset allocation, duration, issuer concentration and liquidity positioning.
•          Optimise risk-adjusted returns while preserving liquidity, quality and eligibility.
•          Oversee portfolio performance, valuation, risk, limits and management information.
•          Ensure effective investment governance, execution controls and escalation.
Accountability:   Stakeholder Engagement
•          Act as a senior Treasury adviser to South African business and executive leadership.
•          Provide concise recommendations to ALCO and relevant governance forums.
•          Engage the Prudential Authority, South African Reserve Bank and industry forums.
•          Work closely with Finance, Risk, Global Markets, Legal, Tax, Compliance, Operations and Internal Audit.
•          Lead and develop a high-performing specialist Treasury team.
Accountability:  Governance & Compliance
•          Operate within approved risk appetite, mandates, limits and delegated authorities.
•          Maintain current policies, processes, controls and governance frameworks.
•          Ensure compliance with prudential, legal, accounting and internal requirements.
•          Oversee data quality, valuation, reporting and relevant model dependencies.
•          Escalate material risks, limit pressures and control weaknesses promptly.
•          Own audit and assurance actions through sustainable closure.
Role/person specification
Preferred Education
• Relevant postgraduate qualification in finance, economics, accounting, quantitative finance or a related discipline.
• CA(SA), CFA or equivalent is advantageous.
Preferred Experience
•          Significant senior experience in Bank treasury, ALM, liquidity, funding, capital or balance sheet management.
•          Demonstrated accountability for material budgets, risk positions and executive decision support.
•          Proven leadership of specialist teams and delivery across complex stakeholder groups.
•          Experience engaging regulators, governance committees and senior executives.
Knowledge and Skills
•          Deep knowledge of South African interest rate, money market and foreign exchange markets.
•          Expertise in HQLA, ALM, liquidity, funding and IRRBB.
•          Strong understanding of capital, RWA, transfer pricing and balance sheet economics.
•          Strategic judgement, commercial acumen and disciplined risk ownership.
•          Clear executive communication, influencing and stakeholder management.
•          Strong people leadership, succession planning and control mindset.
Education
Master's Degree: Business, Commerce and Management Studies

Technology spend → technology performance → customer/business outcome → financial value

text:

With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.

Job Summary
Implementation, monitoring and auditing of Environment, Health and Safety policy, standards and controls within the Absa Group (specifically focused on Absa Building Contractors)
Job Description
Consultant: Occupational Health and Safety
Risk management:
• Ensure compliance with OHS standards and legislation.
• Monitor the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) standards and management information system (MIS) by obtaining quarterly reports from all Absa workplaces.
• Assist regions to become and remain compliant by sending reminders of information that is still outstanding and escalate non-compliance to relevant management structures.
• Liaise with Business Units by providing expert opinions, advice and recommendations pertaining to the OHS Act and COID (Compensation of Injuries and Diseases on duty).
• Engage with various internal Business Units as CRES, Regional Operations, Group Wellness, Human Capital and Group Learning to ensure participation and elimination of risks e.g. noise levels, facility related hazards etc.
• Provide input for training material and present training courses if necessary. Provide facilitators with information when facilitators are not able to respond to a learner’s question. Assist in-country consultants to engage training vendors for courses required for upskilling purposes.
• Conduct site inspections and investigations (e.g. injury on duty investigations) to identify OHS risk related shortcomings and to ensure procedural compliance by staff and contractors. Submit a report on findings. Analyse investigation reports issued by in-country consultants and/or authorities.
• Conduct OHS audits and proactive inspections and report on findings with appropriate recommendations to enhance OHS compliance, which could include, technology, procedural, training or even disciplinary action. Submit a report to the workplace and other affected parties.
• Attend to business unit or region specific meetings and ensure OHS requirements are highlighted and addressed. Attend country legislated OHS Committee Meetings and provide feedback on OHS Compliance from a Centre perspective.
• Assist with development and revision of policies, procedures and standards.
• Assist in-country OHS consultants to compile annual OHS Plans stating objectives to be strategically met in accordance with country legislation, Absa OHS policies and supporting documents. Facilitate approvals of the OHS Plan from senior management in-country and attend to queries in regard to the OHS Plan.
• Assist and advise business on area specific OHS solutions which include; research and development which include the services of technical experts as SABS and occupational hygienists.
• Maintain the OHS SharePoint site to create continual OHS awareness.
• Ensure that all contractors and service providers comply with country legislation by auditing their system to ensure that they take responsibility for staff working for them and that they have valid certification or registration and work procedures in place.
• Monitor OHS implementation at building sites by obtaining and providing information as prescribed by the country (or South African) Construction Regulations which includes the Principal Contractors OHS plan, responsibilities of the Principal contractor, appointments, training, agendas of OHS meeting held, facilities regulations, personal protective equipment etc. Conduct audits of their OHS procedures, do site inspections and attend site safety meetings if required.
Process and Procedure Management for OHS:
• Manage the Occupational Health & Safety system by sending notifications to Managers and OHS Representatives to submit quarterly reports.
• Monitor, manage and provide guidance to all Absa workplaces pertaining to this process. Send out a final reminder to workplaces that failed to submit quarterly reports. Obtain final statistics, compile a quarterly report and escalate non-compliance to various stakeholders.
• Assist in-country consultants to drive compliance by performing audits, inspections and by providing guidance pertaining to appointment of Managers, OHS Representatives, First Aiders, Fire Wardens and Evacuation Leaders.
• Liaise with Group Learning, Line Managers and Regional or relevant in-country Managers to ensure that OHS teams receive the required training and that all AR workplaces conduct physical emergency evacuations at minimum once per annum as prescribed by their legislation.
• Monitor changes in country legislation by receiving changes in legislation from in-country OHS consultants and Legal teams. Assist in-country consultants to compile a legal register for their region and facilitate approval from the in-country legal team.
• Engage in-country OHS consultants for the review of Group OHS policies and supporting documents.
• Manage business unit queries and specific requirements by assessing the risk and providing guidelines for managing the applicable risk within workplaces, projects and events.
Reporting:
• Compile monthly and quarterly risk management reports and submit to Line Manager. Review the in-country OHS Consultant compliance reports prior their presentation in the quarterly OHS committee meetings.
• Escalate non-compliances for OHS System quarterly reports not received, appointments not made and outstanding training requirements to the in-country consultants and People Managers where required.
• Compile adhoc reports as requested by management.
• Compile executive-level reports after visiting countries to provide feedback as to the visit and achievements or issues.
Providing Solutions to ensure OHS compliance:
• Work with various internal and external stakeholders to ensure compliance to eliminate or mitigate risks within the Absa Group. By providing statistics and reports pertaining to non-compliances and incidents.
• Contribute to align policies, supporting procedures and forms to support the prevalent risk reduction and mitigation per workplace.
• Provide guidance and assistance to eliminate or mitigate risks by making use of internal resources, external experts, and in-country authority or Department of Labour approved service providers.
• Be conversant with new technology, training requirements, trends and changes pertaining to OHS matters, to be able to provide clients with solutions.
Communication and Client Service:
• Be available by means of e-mail and cell phone to assist internal and external clients with OHS related matters.
• Provide communication to our audience on Absa Engage and on the OHS SharePoint site.
• Travel to conduct training, premises conformance tests and workplace inspections on request of management or the client to assess current and emerging OHS issues, and facilitate the upskilling and education of in-country OHS consultants.
• Attend meetings to represent Group OHS as a supporting function to AR, as well as attend industry related workshops, conferences, seminars and training sessions to become aware of latest trends and changes.
• Engage in knowledge sharing and collaborative efforts with OHS colleagues and stakeholders.
• Drive viewer engagement and participation for Group-wide physical and virtual OHS campaigns, to promote OHS content. Assist to collaboratively create and develop content for the OHS campaigns.
• Staff in own area (Manager, Group OHS and in-country OHS consultants)
• Staff outside own area (other Centre and AR CRES colleagues)
• Internal customers (OHS Team Members)
• External customers (Group Wellness, Group Learning, Group Legal, Human Capital
• Regulators / Government local authorities
• Vendors / suppliers
• Other (Industry forums / associations)
Experience and Education:
• NQF Level 5 in OHS or equivalent
• Valid Registration with SACPCMP as a CHSO or Candidate CHSO
• Risk assessment, risk management experience and OHS experience up to auditing level
• Incident Investigation certificate or diploma
• SAMTRAC / Nebosh certificate or diploma
• 5 years’ experience in the OHS environment in a major institution, preferably in banking industry or construction industry
• Experience with supervisory and reporting functions
• Effective communication, written and oral skills
• Computer literacy in MS Office applications
• Experience in liaising with external OHS stakeholders
Knowledge and skills:
• Networking with local authorities
• Strong stakeholder management
• Good knowledge of the Occupational Health & Safety legislation
• Audit skills, application of project management methodology and risk management principles
• Must be proficient in analytical risk identification and measurement, as well as risk response strategies
• Self-motivated and take ownership
• Good planning and travel management skills.
• Ability to implement compliance frameworks
Role competencies:
• Establishing rapport with people
• Upholding compliance standards
• Adapting and responding to change
• Adhering to principles and values
• Persuading and influencing
• Relating and networking
• Report writing and data analysis
• Deciding and initiating action
• Planning and organising
Education
Bachelor`s Degrees and Advanced Diplomas: Physical Planning and Construction (Required)

title: Quantitative Analyst - Counterparty Credit Risk DCEM
text:
Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time.
With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Belonging at Absa
Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities. We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Job Summary
•Provide independent analysis and oversight of counterparty credit exposure across derivative portfolios, with a focus on Potential Future Exposure (PFE), mark-to-market (MTM), margin and limit utilization.
•Partner with Front Office, Credit Risk, Quantitative Risk, Finance and Technology teams to support pre-deal assessments, complex transaction analysis and informed credit decisions.
•Maintain a strong control environment by monitoring data quality, investigating exposure exceptions and ensuring that risk information is accurate, complete and appropriately escalated.
•Support the development, testing, validation and ongoing enhancement of counterparty credit risk models, systems and reporting processes, including Sigma, QlikView and associated ETL layers.
•Deliver clear portfolio analytics, stress testing and regulatory or management reporting, while translating technical counterparty credit risk concepts for senior stakeholders and governance forums.
Job Description
Key Accountabilities:
Exposure Management and Credit Analysis
• Calculate, analyse and explain PFE, MTM and related exposure measures for OTC derivatives, Securities Financing Transactions (SFTs), and structured products.
• Support Front Office and Credit Risk stakeholders with pre-deal calculations, ad hoc exposure analysis, limit setting and limit-utilisation queries.
• Assess the drivers of counterparty exposure at trade, netting-set and portfolio level, including the impact of collateral, margining, legal agreements and credit risk mitigation.
• Provide analysis and interpretation of complex transactions to support credit assessments and risk decisions.
• Monitor exposure and limit exceptions, investigate material movements and ensure timely escalation and resolution.
Model, Stress Testing and Risk Analytics
• Develop a sound working knowledge of PFE methodologies, model assumptions and the end-to-end exposure reporting process.
• Collaborate with quantitative and risk teams on model calibration, validation, back-testing and annual model reviews.
• Perform sensitivity analysis, stress testing and scenario analysis to assess the effect of market shocks and adverse conditions on counterparty exposure.
• Produce detailed portfolio analytics, including concentration, sector, wrong-way risk and other relevant counterparty risk views.
• Support stakeholder training and provide clear explanations of exposure methodologies, results and limitations.
Systems, Data and Process Improvement
• Monitor the accuracy and completeness of exposure data through effective data-quality controls, reconciliations, reporting and escalation.
• Assist with user acceptance testing for Sigma releases, model enhancements and other system changes.
• Provide clear business requirements to Technology teams and support testing, implementation and issue resolution.
• Help maintain and improve the existing risk system framework, including Sigma, QlikView models and relevant ETL processes.
• Identify opportunities to automate and streamline reporting, manual overrides, marginal risking and other recurring processes, while supporting strategic solutions.
• Document processes, methodologies, controls, test results and model changes to an appropriate audit and governance standard.
Reporting, Governance and Stakeholder Engagement
• Prepare accurate and timely regular and ad hoc counterparty credit risk reports for management, governance forums and regulatory authorities.
• Support daily margin reporting to the Prudential Authority and monthly stress-testing, scenario-analysis, KRI and management-information reporting.
• Prepare concise presentations and commentary that explain key exposure movements, concentrations, emerging risks and control matters.
• Represent the team in counterparty credit risk workstreams and contribute PFE and MTM considerations to cross-functional discussions.
• Maintain awareness of relevant market developments, regulatory changes and industry practice, including SA-CCR and margin requirements.
• Accuracy, completeness and timeliness of counterparty exposure analysis and reporting.
• Effective identification, investigation and escalation of data, model, system and limit issues.
• Clear ownership of assigned deliverables and adherence to governance, control and documentation standards.
• Constructive collaboration with stakeholders across Front Office, Credit Risk, Quantitative Risk and Technology.
Required Qualifications and Experience
• Bachelor's Degree or Advanced Diploma in Risk Management, Financial Risk Management, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics or a related quantitative discipline.
• One to three years of relevant experience in counterparty credit risk, derivatives or quantitative risk.
• Working knowledge of financial markets, derivative products, exposure measurement and risk metrics.
• Professional qualifications such as FRM or CA(SA) are advantageous.
• Exposure to counterparty credit risk regulation, including SA-CCR and margin requirements, is advantageous.
Technical Skills and Knowledge
• Understanding of counterparty credit risk concepts, including netting, collateral, legal agreements, margining and credit risk mitigation.
• Ability to interpret complex datasets, perform root-cause analysis and translate results into practical risk insights.
• Advanced Excel capability; experience with Power BI, Python, SQL or other automation and analytics tools is advantageous.
• Experience with risk systems, data visualisation tools and data-processing workflows; Sigma and QlikView exposure is advantageous.
• Knowledge of model governance, validation, back-testing, stress testing and data-quality control principles.
Behavioural Competencies
• Strong analytical judgement, attention to detail and a disciplined approach to controls.
• Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences.
• Proactive, self-motivated and accountable, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
• Collaborative and solutions-focused, with the confidence to challenge constructively and escalate when required.
• Curious and improvement-oriented, with a commitment to developing technical and regulatory knowledge.
Key Stakeholders
• Front Office and Trading Desks
• Credit Risk and Counterparty Credit Risk teams
• Quantitative Risk and Model Validation
• Technology, Data and Infrastructure teams
• Regulatory Reporting, senior management and governance forums
Education
Bachelor`s Degrees and Advanced Diplomas: Business, Commerce and Management Studies (Required)

title: Transaction Manager
text:
Job Description
To support in the execution of and management of financial transactions adhering to regulatory compliance and defined policies and procedures.
To play a crucial role in ensuring accurate deal booking and adherence to established processes within the organisation’s Transaction Management function. Mitigate operational and reputational risk by validating the quality and accuracy of transaction data, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements, and supporting effective risk management practices.
To collaborate with various stakeholders, including traders, risk management teams, and back-office processing functions, to uphold data integrity, streamline processes, and enhance the overall efficiency and accuracy of transaction management. • Conduct detailed reviews of transaction data to identify discrepancies, verify completeness, and ensure data integrity within transaction systems, thus supporting reliable financial reporting.
• Engage in the due diligence process by compiling the necessary documentation and liaising with relevant advisors.
• Act as a key point of contact, addressing inquiries, providing updates, and ensuring a high level of service throughout the transaction process to maintain client satisfaction and trust.
• Monitor and ensure all transactions adhere to internal policies and external regulatory requirements, including KYC (Know Your Customer) and AML (Anti-Money Laundering) standards, to prevent legal and financial penalties.
• Assist in the execution of transactions, coordinating closing logistics, finalising documentation, and ensuring all procedural requirements are met for successful transaction completion.
• Validate that all transactions are booked accurately and in line with client instructions and regulatory requirements to minimise booking errors and reduce operational risk.
• Identify and flags any inconsistencies or irregularities in transaction data, escalating issues promptly to mitigate financial and reputational risk.
• Attend DCF's for all new deals and comment on Legal Agreements and ensure that the legal agreements can be operationalised.
• Engage with the Deal Team and the TM to ensure that deal intention is understood and that Transaction Management can provide the support required to implement the deal and conduct the ongoing maintenance required.
• Ensure processes are followed and backdate approval is required where necessary.
• Ensure New Deal implementation is approved according to Legals and the DCF.
• Reconcile transaction records across different systems to confirm data consistency and integrity across platforms.
• Participate in projects aimed at improving transaction management processes, focusing on automation, accuracy, and efficiency to enhance data quality standards.
• Communicate transaction data quality insights to internal stakeholders, including traders and risk managers, ensuring transparency and promoting proactive issue resolution.
• Develop and monitor key metrics for data quality within the transaction management function, ensuring consistent and quantifiable improvement.
• Identify and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and client service in transaction management data quality, contributing to operational excellence.
• Track and report on transaction-related risks, collaborating with senior managers to develop and implement effective risk mitigation strategies.
• Collaborate with internal teams i.e., legal, compliance, credit, and operations to ensure cohesive and efficient transaction management.
• Engage in ongoing training and development activities to build expertise in transaction management
• Build and sustain collaborative working relationships with relevant peers and stakeholders to achieve productivity synergies.
• Participate in specialist communities of practice and contribute positively to own and organisational knowledge improvement.

title: Client Service Priority Consultant
text:
Job Description
Dear Future Client Service Priority Consultant,
RMB is a place where exceptional people create their own opportunities by challenging the conventional and driving sustainable impact.
United by our proud heritage and strong ethics. Innovative ideas, it’s the magic of our people and culture that sets us apart.
Now, is the time to imagine your next move with South Africa’s number one employer in Financial Services for 2025, where you can embrace the power of collective thinking to unlock unique opportunities for our clients and society.
This role entails providing dedicated, expedited services to priority clients, ensuring their needs are met promptly and effectively. Operating across various client communication channels and prioritise queries, resolve issues and coordinate with internal teams to provide exceptional client experiences. Maintain and strengthening long-term priority relationships and promote loyalty to the organisation. Are You Someone Who Can:
• Service and the primary point of contact for Priority Clients, delivering personalised and expedited service through various client communication channels.
• Prioritise incoming inquires and requests from Priority Clients, ensuring swift resolution and timely responses.
• Anticipate client needs and proactively address potential issues or concerns.
• Proactively identify opportunities to cross-sell or upsell based on client needs and preferences.
• Liaise with internal stakeholders, including product specialists and relationship managers to expedite solutions and ensure seamless client experiences.
• Advocate for Priority Clients within the organisation, escalating issues and advocating for solutions that align with client expectations and company policies.
• Monitor SLAs and performance metrics to track response times and service quality, identifying opportunities for improvement
• Conduct regular check-ins with Priority Clients to gather feedback, address concerns and identify opportunities to enhance the client experience.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to streamline processes, eliminate bottlenecks, and optimise efficiency in serving priority clients.
• Stay informed about industry trends, market developments to anticipate client needs and recommend relevant solutions.

title: Non-Bank ALM Risk Head
text:
Job Description
To lead the Asset and Liability Management (ALM) Risk function for insurance and other non-bank businesses within Group Treasury Risk, ensuring that ALM risks are proactively identified, assessed, measured, monitored, managed, and reported in an accurate and timely manner. The role provides independent oversight of the ALM risk framework, ensuring adherence to Group policies, approved risk limits, governance standards, and risk appetite requirements, while supporting effective risk management and regulatory compliance across the non-bank portfolio. • Build and enhance forward-looking ALM risk modelling capabilities, including scenario analysis and stress testing.
• Monitor industry trends, regulatory developments, and international best practices to improve ALM risk management practices.
• Assess the impact of regulatory and legislative changes and provide input into relevant risk management frameworks.
• Ensure that insurance and non-bank ALM risk appetite measures remain appropriate in the context of business strategy, operating conditions, regulatory requirements, and overall organisational risk appetite.
• Continuously enhance ALM risk frameworks, policies, methodologies, and management practices to improve risk maturity and effectiveness.
• Ensure compliance with approved risk appetite measures, prudential requirements, and relevant governance standards.
• Maintain an effective ALM control environment and promote a strong risk culture across insurance and non-bank businesses.
• Anticipate emerging ALM risks and work collaboratively with first-line teams to address and mitigate risk exposures.
• Provide independent oversight, challenge, and guidance to business stakeholders on ALM risk matters.
• Develop, maintain, and enhance ALM risk metrics, measurement methodologies, and risk management approaches.
• Oversee the preparation and review of ALM risk reports for risk monitoring, governance committees, and internal and external stakeholders.
• Establish standards and expectations for ALM risk information presented to governance forums.
• Support the effective functioning of ALM governance, oversight processes, and committees.
• Build and maintain effective relationships with key stakeholders, including business leadership, Board committees, ALCCO, regulators, and other relevant parties.
• Communicate ALM risk exposures, trends, and key matters clearly and transparently to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Lead, coach, and develop a team of ALM risk professionals to deliver effective risk oversight and support.
• Foster a culture of learning, collaboration, accountability, and continuous professional development.
• Support succession planning and capability development within the ALM Risk function.
• Manage employee performance through clear goal setting, coaching, feedback, and development planning.
• Participate in talent management and people practices in accordance with organisational policies and procedures.

title: Senior Commission Analyst
text:
Senior Commission Analyst
Overview
The Senior Commission Analyst will play a lead role in the calculation, analysis, and maintenance of the sales compensation plan, in addition to supporting the annual planning process. This role sits within the Sales Operations team and partners closely with Sales Operations leadership, Finance, GTM, and Human Resources to administer sales compensation plans. The Senior Commission Analyst acts as a key liaison between Sales Operations, Finance, and internal IT/systems teams, and supports expense accrual planning and ongoing maintenance of commissions processes and systems as part of the global commissions team.
Key Responsibilities
• Calculate and validate commission accruals and payments on a monthly basis, ensuring accuracy and timeliness.
• Assist with commissions system maintenance and updates, including validating calculations and supporting configuration changes, as part of the global commissions team.

• Maintain processes for spiff management, role changes, and sales compensation documentation.
• Support the annual planning process through analysis of commission expense trends.

title: Change Analyst
text:
SS&C is a leading provider of mission-critical, AI-powered technology and services empowering financial services and healthcare organizations to work smarter, faster, and securely. Founded in 1986, SS&C is headquartered in Windsor, Connecticut, and has offices worldwide. More than 23,000 financial services and healthcare organizations, from the world's largest companies to small and mid-market firms, rely on SS&C for expertise, scale, and technology.
Job Description
Change Analyst
Location : Belville, South Africa | Hybrid
Why You Will Love It Here!
• Flexibility : Hybrid Work Model
• Work/Life Balance: Flexible Personal/Vacation Time Off, Sick Leave, Paid Holidays
• Your Wellbeing: Medical, Vision, Employee Assistance Program, Parental Leave
• Diversity & Inclusion: Committed to Welcoming, Celebrating and Thriving on Diversity
• Training: Hands-On, Team-Customized, including SS&C University
Get To Know The Team:
Our team is seeking a detail-oriented Change Analyst to support and facilitate effective change management processes across the organization. This role involves analyzing change requests, assessing impact, and ensuring smooth implementation across various systems and departments.
What You Will Get To Do
• Receive, review, and analyze change requests, ensuring completeness and adherence to established protocols.
• Collaborate with stakeholders (IT, business units, project managers) to understand the scope and impact of proposed changes.
• Perform impact assessments to identify potential risks, dependencies, and resource requirements associated with changes.
• Facilitate change advisory board (CAB) meetings, preparing agendas, documenting discussions, and tracking action items.
• Maintain and update the change management system, ensuring accurate and up-to-date records of all change activities.
• Monitor the implementation of approved changes, ensuring compliance with scheduled timelines and quality standards.
• Communicate change statuses, upcoming changes, and potential disruptions to relevant stakeholders.
• Identify and recommend improvements to the change management process and tools.
• Assist in the development and delivery of training materials related to change management procedures.
• Generate reports on change activity, success rates, and compliance metrics.
What You Will Bring
• Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field.
• 4+ years of experience in a change management, IT support, or project coordination role, preferably within a financial services or technology environment.
• Strong understanding of the financial services industry, particularly asset management and end-to-end back-office administration processes.
• Sound knowledge of fund administration, investment products, portfolio administration, and corporate actions.
• Familiarity with financial instruments traded across capital markets, including equities, fixed income, derivatives, and money market instruments.
• Ability to assess the impact of proposed changes on investment operations, back-office workflows, and related systems.
• Strong understanding of IT service management (ITSM) principles and frameworks (e.g., ITIL Foundation certification preferred).
• Proficiency with change management software and tools (e.g., ServiceNow, Jira, etc.).
• Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with a keen eye for detail.
• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex information clearly.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
• Demonstrated ability to assess risk and make informed decisions.

• Work in an Agile environment, participating in sprint planning, stand-ups and retrospectives.

Partner with DevOps on reliable environments, containerised execution and production-like test data.

Analyse unstable tests and continuously improve framework reliability, execution performance and reporting quality.

Lead performance and reliability-testing initiatives using k6 or comparable tooling.

Ensure non-functional risks are included in release-quality decisions.

Hands-on expertise with Playwright and modern UI and API automation practices.

title: OTC Trader
text:
About us:
Luno is the crypto investment app you can rely on, enabling you to buy, store and explore crypto securely. We’re committed to putting the power of cryptocurrency in everyone's hands sensibly and responsibly.
Since 2013, we’ve helped millions of people around the world invest safely in crypto. We do this by cutting through the hype and supporting customers at every step of the way. All products and cryptocurrencies on our platform must first meet stringent legal, risk and technical security standards.
Transparency is key for us. Luno stores all crypto on a 1:1 basis and we have rigorous processes in place so you can be confident your investment is secure. We’re available in more than 40 countries around the world and we work closely with respective regulators in all of these markets to be fully compliant, as we believe this is the best way to help everyone, everywhere, invest safely.
The role in a nutshell:
This is a front-line trading seat on Luno's OTC desk in South Africa, reporting to the Head of Trading. You'll price, execute and risk-manage large trades for customers who already trade with us in size — institutions, corporates and professional traders — in one of the world's most active crypto-fiat markets. Sitting within our Treasury team, you'll work with the rest of the OTC desk, in-country teams and relationship managers to turn that flow into a consistently profitable book.
It's a mid-level role built to grow. We intend to lead every market we operate in, and we're building the desk's future leadership from within: you'll start by running South African flow, take on new markets and strategies as we expand, and step toward senior desk leadership as the trading business scales. If your ambition is to one day run a desk, this is where you build the track record and client franchise to get there.
Your mission will be:
- Own the client book
• Be the voice of the desk for institutional customers and VIP traders: price and quote large OTC trades, source counter-trades, and execute with speed and discipline.
• Build durable relationships with those clients alongside our country teams and relationship managers — the goal is repeat flow, not one-off tickets.
• Manage the desk's working capital, ensuring anticipated trades are pre-funded or backed by adequate credit facilities.
• Own trade disputes end-to-end, and work with Trade Operations to settle every trade cleanly.
- Run execution and risk
• Execute across the book — OTC trades, counter-trades, and market counter-trades when matched flow falls through — always within approved trading strategies.
• Hedge Luno's market risk on its working capital and revenue streams, and execute revenue liquidation trades.
• Own the desk's P&L against targets and risk limits — you'll know your numbers cold and be able to defend every line of them.
- Shape trading strategy
• Drive the development of trading strategies across crypto and FX — OTC, hedging and revenue liquidation today; derivatives, arbitrage and warehousing as the desk matures — with risk management and profitability at the core.
- Read the market
• Produce in-depth analysis of digital asset markets: trends, opportunities and risks, plus the news, regulatory shifts and flows that move prices.
• Deliver the daily market read to the Treasury team, and push your insights into decisions made across Luno.
- Report with rigour
• Maintain accurate records of trades, P&L, risk and performance metrics — an auditable book is a credible book.
• Produce regular stakeholder reporting on trading activity, performance and market insight.
- Build the desk
• Spec improvements to Luno's trading and risk systems and shape our push into automation — helping us evolve from manual execution to a scaled, systematic operation.
• Pressure-test our risk frameworks and models, and make the case for changes as market dynamics shift.
A little about you:
• 3–5 years of trading experience within a sell-side OTC desk, market maker, prop desk or brokerage in crypto (preferred), FX, equities or derivatives.
• Your trading experience includes P/L responsibility based on Trade and Counter-trade within trade size limits, position limits, working capital etc (this is an OTC principal trader role rather than an execution trader role).
• Bachelor's in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Business Administration, Accounting or related discipline.
• Derivatives arbitrage knowledge or experience would be a plus.
• An advanced degree or professional qualification (CFA, CAIA, MBA) in a related field is beneficial.
• A successful broking / OTC trading track record across more than one market.
• Ambition to grow with the desk — you see this role as a step toward broader market ownership and, in time, trading leadership.
• Ability to adapt to a fast-paced and dynamic trading environment.
• Compliance with regulatory standards and a commitment to ethical trading practices.
• Strong attention to detail and accuracy in trade execution and documentation.
• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, a strong team player.
• Friendly, transparent, articulate and driven to succeed.
• A passion for crypto.
Life at Luno:
• Remote but reachable work policy gives you the freedom to choose between working from home or the office.
• Plus the option to buy and sell up to 5 days leave
• Improve body and mind, with excellent private medical insurance
• Retirement fund benefit helping you build the financial foundation you need to enjoy your future to the fullest.
• Access to Learnably and our additional learning platforms for your personal and professional development

• Paw-ternity leave for your furry friend

• Free lunch and snacks
• 0 fees up to a certain amount with Luno from the day you start.*

title: Senior Manager, Corporate FP&A
text:
At 2U, we are all in on purpose. We are motivated by our mission – to make learning limitless– and connected by our shared passion to deliver world-class higher education at scale. As the parent company of edX, a leading online learning platform, 2U powers thousands of higher education offerings – from free courses to full degrees. Together with our college, university, and corporate partners, we are helping accelerate careers and transform lives.
What We’re Looking For:
The Finance team at 2U provides strategic financial leadership and analytical support to stakeholders across the organization. We support decision-making and operational effectiveness through financial planning, analysis, and cross-functional collaboration, all in service of 2U’s mission to expand access to high-quality education.
As a Senior Manager, FP&A, you will serve as 2U’s lead Workday Adaptive Planning superuser and financial model builder, owning the backend planning infrastructure that powers our corporate forecasting. In this role, you will play a critical, hands-on role supporting high-impact initiatives across the business—building dynamic three-statement models, evaluating new initiatives, supporting business case development, driving financial modeling, and surfacing insights that inform company-wide decisions. You’ll work closely with Finance leadership and cross-functional teams to drive clarity around priorities, risks, and opportunities.
This is an ideal role for a highly analytical and proactive individual with strong business acumen and a desire to work in a mission-driven and fast-paced environment.
Responsibilities Include, But Are Not Limited To:
Financial Planning, Forecasting & Strategic Analysis
• Help lead the annual operating plan, monthly forecasting, and long-range planning processes across the organization.
• Own the consolidation of enterprise financial forecasts, budgets, and long-range plans across all business units, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and consistency of financial assumptions.
• Develop and maintain integrated three-statement financial models (income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow) to support planning, liquidity management, and executive decision-making.
• Build scenario analyses, business cases, and financial models to evaluate strategic initiatives, investments, and operational decisions.
• Partner with executive leadership to identify risks, opportunities, and actionable recommendations that support company objectives.
Business Partnership & Performance Management
• Partner with business leaders to evaluate financial performance, operational trends, and resource allocation.
• Analyze monthly financial results, identify key performance drivers, and communicate actionable insights to leadership.
• Develop scalable reporting, dashboards, and KPIs to monitor business performance and improve decision-making.
• Support cross-functional initiatives by providing financial analysis and decision support.
FP&A Systems, Reporting & Process Improvement
• Lead continuous improvements to FP&A processes, reporting, and planning capabilities through automation and standardization.
• Maintain and enhance financial planning models and reporting within Adaptive Planning, ensuring data integrity, forecasting accuracy, and efficient planning processes.
• Improve financial reporting infrastructure and documentation to increase transparency and scalability.
• Prepare executive, Board, and management reporting materials that clearly communicate financial performance and outlook.
Strategic Initiatives & Partner Finance Support
• Lead or support enterprise strategic initiatives requiring cross-functional financial evaluation and coordination.
• Support Degree partner cash collection initiatives through financial analysis, reporting, forecasting, and collaboration with business partners to improve working capital and cash flow.
• Provide ad hoc financial analyses to support evolving business priorities during the company's transformation.
Leadership & Team Development
• Foster a high-performance culture grounded in accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
• Elevate analytical capabilities, financial acumen, and storytelling skills across the team.
• Optimize team structure and workflows to scale with company growth.
Things That Should Be In Your Background:
• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field (MBA preferred)
• 10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, corporate finance, or related field, with 5+ years in a leadership role
• Demonstrated experience managing and developing high-performing teams
• Strong executive presence with the ability to communicate financial insights
• Advanced proficiency with Adaptive Planning (or comparable enterprise planning systems) including model development, forecasting, reporting, and administration
• Advanced financial modeling and analytical skills
• Demonstrated competency in three-statement financial modeling
• Proven ability to translate complex financial analyses into clear, compelling narratives for Board and executive-level presentations
Working Conditions:
• 5% of travel via plane, car, and train may be required
• Flexibility to work more than 40 hours per week when business needs warrant
Physical Requirements
• Mobility within the office including movement from floor to floor
• Access information using a computer
Benefits & Culture
Our global employee base is a diverse collection of innovators, dreamers, and doers working together to transform lives through higher education. We believe that every employee can advance our shared purpose, and that life at 2U should be fun and meaningful. If you’re excited by the opportunity to provide millions of learners and counting with access to world-class higher education, then join us – and do work that makes a difference.
We offer comprehensive benefits (unique per country) and excellent work/life balance.
Full-time, U.S. benefits include:
• Medical, dental, and vision coverage
• Life insurance, disability, and 401(k) employer match
• Free snacks and drinks in-office
• Generous paid holidays and leave policies, including unlimited PTO
• Additional time off benefits include: volunteer days, parental leave, and a company-wide winter break
The anticipated base salary range for this role is ($125,000 - $150,000), with potential bonus eligibility. Salary offers are made based on the candidate’s qualifications, experience, skills, and education as they directly relate to the requirements of the position, budget for the position and cost of labor in the market in which the candidate will be hired.
2U Diversity and Inclusion Statement
At 2U, we are committed to building and sustaining a culture of belonging, respect, and inclusion. We are proud of the steps we’ve taken to bring together an employee base that embodies diverse walks of life, ideas, genders, ages, races, cultures, sexual orientations, abilities and other unique qualities. We strive to offer a workplace where every employee feels empowered by what makes us different, as well as by how we are alike.
2U is committed to providing reasonable accommodations during our recruitment process. If you need assistance or accommodations, please reach out to us at: recruitingaccommodations@2u.com .
About 2U
2U partners with the world's top universities and companies to develop and deliver education programs that accelerate careers and transform lives. Through partnerships with the world’s leading colleges, universities, and companies, 2U delivers thousands of online programs to millions of learners worldwide on edX, its global learning platform. From executive education and professional credentialing to master’s degree programs and free, open courses, 2U transforms how top institutions deliver workforce-aligned online education, enabling professionals to advance without pausing their careers. Learn more at 2U.com.

All employees may be required to perform duties outside of their normal responsibilities from time to time, as needed.

• Strong sales and relationship-building skills
• Excellent verbal and written communication
• Entrepreneurial thinking with a self-motivated, target-driven mindset
• Strong negotiation and influencing skills
• Professionalism, integrity, and a customer-focused attitude
• Ability to manage multiple stakeholders and navigate complex applications

• Access to training, tools, and support to ensure optimal deal closure and client service

title: Education Portfolio Manager
text:
Let's Write Africa's Story Together!
Old Mutual is a firm believer in the African opportunity and our diverse talent reflects this.
Job Description
Lead the design, implementation and continuous improvement of the Foundation’s Education portfolio, translating the strategy into measurable school-level impact. The role connects needs-led school support, high-quality implementation partnerships and supports employee volunteerism so that interventions are practical, evidence-informed, scalable and responsive to local context.
Key Result Areas
Strategy and portfolio leadership
• Own the Education portfolio implementation roadmap and translate strategic objectives into annual plans, priorities, milestones and measurable outcomes.
• Guide the phased three-year rollout, ensuring implementation choices reflect provincial context, school need, feasibility, additionality and available resources.
• Use clear selection and intervention criteria to prioritise support that addresses evidenced school and learner needs rather than applying a one-size-fits-all model.
• Continuously review the portfolio against emerging evidence, implementation learning and the Foundation’s strategic intent, and recommend course corrections where required.
• Programme design and delivery
• Lead end-to-end programme design and delivery, from needs assessment and solution design through contracting, implementation, handover and close-out.
• Oversee education interventions that strengthen learning conditions and outcomes, including appropriate literacy, numeracy, teacher-support and enabling school interventions where these align to assessed need.
• Coordinate school-level implementation so that partner activity, employee volunteerism opportunities and learner-facing engagements are sequenced effectively and do not disrupt teaching and learning.
Partnerships and stakeholder management
• Build and manage strategic relationships with schools, implementation partners, education stakeholders and relevant government structures, including the Department of Basic Education and provincial education authorities where appropriate.
• Identify partnership opportunities that strengthen reach, quality, sustainability or system alignment.
• Lead partner scoping and onboarding from a programme perspective, defining deliverables, roles, safeguards, reporting requirements and escalation pathways.
• Represent the Education portfolio credibly in senior stakeholder engagements, sector forums and internal governance processes.
Measurement, learning and reporting
• Define programme-level outputs, outcomes and indicators aligned to the strategy and ensure reliable baseline, implementation and outcome data are available for decision-making.
• Monitor delivery quality, learner and school reach, partner performance, implementation risks and progress against agreed milestones and budgets.
• Turn monitoring insights into practical improvements and clearly communicate performance, lessons, risks and decisions required to leadership and governance forums.
• Maintain a credible evidence base showing what was funded, who was reached, what changed and where the Foundation’s contribution added value.
• Governance, risk and financial management
• Manage the Education portfolio within approved budgets, delegations, procurement requirements and finance and risk governance.
• Ensure programme and partner decisions are supported by appropriate due diligence, contracting, safeguarding, evidence and approval processes.
• Maintain oversight of delivery dependencies, reputational and implementation risks, and escalate material issues early with recommended mitigation actions.
• People and cross-functional leadership
• Contribute to functional resource planning and coordinate internal and external resources required for successful delivery.
• Provide clear direction, prioritisation and quality assurance to assigned staff and service providers, with accountability for performance and outputs.
• Collaborate across Foundation, GSI and relevant business teams to align implementation, stakeholder engagement, communications and employee participation.
Qualifications, Skills and Experience:
• Relevant degree in Education, Development Studies, Social Science, Community Development or a related field.
• At least 5 years’ relevant experience managing education or social investment programmes, preferably within the South African education system.
• Demonstrated programme and project management capability, including multi-site or multi-partner implementation.
• Strategic planning experience with the ability to translate strategy into practical delivery plans and measurable outcomes.
• Experience managing partners, senior stakeholders and service providers; people-management experience is advantageous as the role has direct reports.
• Strong analytical capability, including interpretation of programme data, needs assessments, education evidence and policy.
• Working knowledge of monitoring, evaluation and learning, budgeting, risk management, due diligence and governance in a social-investment environment.
• Strong written, presentation and facilitation skills, with confidence engaging senior decisionmakers and public-sector stakeholders.
• Experience in literacy, numeracy, teacher development or whole-school support is advantageous.
• Proficiency in one or more South African languages in addition to English is advantageous.
• Additional Requirements:
• Regular travel to schools and partner sites, including rural and peri-urban locations.
• Valid driver’s licence and access to reliable transport, in line with organisational travel requirements.
